people.name: Alan Mathison Turing
people.summary: Alan Turing was an English mathematician and pioneer of theoretical computer science and artificial intelligence. He formalized the concepts of algorithm and computation with the Turing machine, played a crucial role in Allied codebreaking during World War II at Bletchley Park, designed early stored-program computer architecture at the National Physical Laboratory, and later contributed foundational ideas to morphogenesis.

people.name: Alan_Turing
people.summary: Alan Turing was an English mathematician and pioneering computer scientist whose 1936 formulation of the Turing machine shaped theoretical computer science. During World War II he led key cryptanalytic work at Bletchley Park, and later designed early stored-program computer architectures and published influential papers on artificial intelligence and morphogenesis.

people.name: Augusta Ada King, Countess of Lovelace
people.summary: Augusta Ada King, Countess of Lovelace, also known as Ada Lovelace, was an English mathematician and writer chiefly known for her work on Charles Babbage's proposed mechanical general-purpose computer, the Analytical Engine. She was the first to recognise that the machine had applications beyond pure calculation and is sometimes considered the first computer programmer.

people.name: Emmy Noether
people.summary: Amalie Emmy Noether was a German mathematician who fundamentally transformed abstract algebra and proved Noether's theorems linking symmetries to conservation laws in physics. A leading figure at Göttingen, she developed deep theories of rings, fields, and algebras, and later taught in the United States at Bryn Mawr College while conducting research at the Institute for Advanced Study.

people.name: Henry II, Holy Roman Emperor
people.summary: Henry II (Saint Henry) was Holy Roman Emperor from 1014 to 1024 and the last ruler of the Ottonian dynasty. Rising from Duke of Bavaria (995), he secured the German throne in 1002, became King of Italy in 1004, and was crowned emperor by Pope Benedict VIII in 1014. A pious ruler closely allied with the Church, he founded the Diocese of Bamberg, promoted monastic reform, and consolidated imperial authority north of the Alps. Dying childless in 1024, he was canonized in 1146.
